extracted.intended_audience: actors, comedians, and TV production readers interested in improvised television comedy
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and practical norms for producing and performing on an outline-driven, largely improvised television comedy (as practiced on Curb Your Enthusiasm): how episodes are prepared, how actors audition and perform, and how directors manage spontaneity and takes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episodes outlined but not scripted
rubrics_metrics.description: Episodes are outlined (about seven pages long) and are essentially the story of the show; not very much of it is dialogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actors work from the outline rather than a full script — they 'know the story and know what has to be said' and then improvise dialogue. Example: Jeff Garlin said the outline is seven pages and may include only one written line for an actor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spontaneity of the moment
rubrics_metrics.description: Performers should avoid pre-planning lines or overthinking; spontaneity is central.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-writing or rehearsing specific lines is 'the enemy.' Even after multiple takes and angles, actors should aim to be as spontaneous as the first take. Anti-pattern: preparing set lines before shooting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom to improvise (may change storyline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Actors have the freedom to improvise material that can substantively alter the storyline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While improvisation can change plot elements, actors should recognize when something 'is working' and avoid needlessly changing it. Use improvisation strategically and collaboratively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial and error; many takes
rubrics_metrics.description: The production uses tremendous trial and error, taking many takes to explore options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect 'take after take after take' to try different approaches. Directors and actors use multiple attempts to discover the funniest or most truthful moments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actors expected to create characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Larry relies on the ability of hired performers to come in and create characters rather than being fully prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actors should develop distinct character choices and bring them into the improvisation; creating a believable character helps generate organic comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplined yet flexible set
rubrics_metrics.description: The set is disciplined and flexible in equal measure — there is structure but room for experimentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance following the episode's story needs (discipline) with trying unexpected beats (flexibility). This structure supports improv while keeping the episode coherent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improv audition with need-to-know information
rubrics_metrics.description: Guest actors often audition via an improv session with Larry, receiving only a brief synopsis/backstory and limited information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auditions test an actor's ability to think on their feet with minimal context; directors operate on a 'need-to-know' basis to preserve spontaneity. Prepare to perform with sparse prep.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounded performance even in absurdity
rubrics_metrics.description: Performances should be grounded in reality even when the situation or character is absurd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid being 'too jokey'; commit to realistic choices that make absurd lines or situations land. Example: Chris Williams emphasized staying grounded in his audition despite absurdity.

rubrics_metrics.name: A-list guests may still audition
rubrics_metrics.description: High-profile guest stars are often required to audition for their parts unless they are playing themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume celebrity status exempts you from testing; be prepared to improvise in an audition setting unless cast to appear as oneself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Occasional scripted lines from creator
rubrics_metrics.description: The creator/director may provide one or a few specific lines for an actor to say in an episode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept and incorporate occasional scripted beats (e.g., 'I may get one line that Larry will write per episode') while improvising the rest of the performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity when playing yourself
rubrics_metrics.description: When guests are cast to play themselves, they are often told simply to 'be you.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authentic behavior can be the directive for non-actor personalities; however, expect the production to ask for particular interactions or reactions to keep the scene dynamic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain spontaneity across multiple angles/takes
rubrics_metrics.description: Even with repeated takes and different camera angles, performers must strive to preserve the spontaneity that produced the original comedic moment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat each take as an opportunity to recreate the immediacy of the first performance; directors will use multiple angles but value fresh, spontaneous delivery each time.
